messages:
sara lim: CI perf alert on PR 21876 — microbench `batcher_latency` exceeded threshold on blocker job. Job: https://ci.internal/redwood/21876/123

Failing metric: p95 latency went from 12.3ms -> 18.9ms (threshold 15.0ms). Artifact: s3://ci-artifacts/21876/batcher_latency/trace.zip

This PR touched the gating heuristics in scheduler (file: batcher/heuristics.py). Could be kernel selection fallout or gating weight change. Can someone triage?

ben cho: Repro locally? Try: `PYTHONPATH=./srv pytest tests/perf/test_batcher.py::test_batcher_latency --bench --runs 20`. Also run the microbench harness: `./tools/perf/microbench --bench batcher_latency --model gpt2-small`

yun park: I pulled the artifact and ran a perf sample. Flamegraph/top shows a big jump in kernel selection work. Short summary:
```
kernel_selector.select_best_kernel  48.2%
batcher._compute_window          12.4%
kv_cache.lookup                   6.5%
other                             33%
```
Looks like `select_best_kernel` spends more time scoring candidates after the change in heuristics.

infra-bot: CI captured perf artifacts and traces: https://ci.internal/artifacts/21876/trace.zip. Snapshot id: prod-ci-20260319-1422.

mike jenkins: If it's kernel scoring, bisect the commits touching heuristics + autoselect. Quick bisect command: `tools/ci/bisect_perf.sh --metric batcher_latency --bench test_batcher_latency --range a1b2c3..d4e5f6` (replace range with last known good). Last known good tag: v1.12.3.

anya ivanova: Ran a focused local bisect on `main` between v1.12.3..HEAD (range a1b2..f7g8). Culprit commit: d3f9c7 (merge of #21650). That merge adjusted sample weighting in the gating heuristic and also pulled in a small kernel-autoselect tweak. Reverting d3f9c7 locally drops p95 back to ~12.6ms.

sara lim: Can you paste the minimal diff that caused it?

anya ivanova: Minimal diff snippet from heuristics.py:
```
-    weight = seq_len * 1.0
+    weight = seq_len * 1.2
```
Also kernel selector added a soft-penalty for short sequences in the same PR. Together they increase scoring attempts for some inputs.

ben cho: Nice find. Could we patch the selector to early-exit instead of full revert? That might be lower-risk than reverting the whole merge.

anya ivanova: Patch is small but the merge touched other refactors. Given this is a rollout blocker for prod latency, my recommendation: revert merge, run CI, then reintroduce targeted fix with microbench coverage.

sara lim: Agree. I'll open a revert PR and set it as rollout blocker. Starting revert now. Linking here when done.

ben cho: If you open the revert, please trigger the perf job with `--collect-artifacts` so we have golden traces. Also tag @eng-oncall if we need fast rollback. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Deploy gate updated: `batcher_latency` suite flagged. New blocker set by sara lim.

sara lim: Revert PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/pulls/21901 (WIP). Marked for immediate review and perf run. Will post CI link shortly.

mike jenkins: After revert and green perf, we can create a follow-up PR that reintroduces the kernel-autoselect tweak behind a flag and add a perf test covering the seq_len weighting.

sara lim: Sounds good. For tracking: created a brief runbook note in the PR description with the bisect steps and local repro commands.

ben cho: Thanks all — ping me if revert CI flakes, I'll help triage.

infra-bot: Note: rollout remains blocked until `batcher_latency` passes on main.
